src: Ejercito Argentino, Fichas de enrolamiento, Cajon 985 (Lera) — image group 112342450
what: Pablo Armando's own enrolment card
got: His father and mother, named. The one search on this page that answered the central question

src: Rosario cathedral, Indice de bautismos before 1879 — eighty openings read by eye
what: The surname, before the window everything else had started from
got: One Lerena in a hundred and forty-eight years of one parish

src: Rosario cathedral, death index — the biggest untried set there
what: Deaths, where every sweep before had been baptisms and marriages
got: It answers two thirds of the question and then runs out of pages

src: Rosario cathedral register, read act by act to 750 acts
what: Whether the 1945 typescript index can be trusted at all — every Rosario null here rests on it
got: The index held. The nulls built on it stand

src: FamilySearch /search/ endpoints
what: Continuing the pre-1879 read
got: Firewalled mid-session. Recorded as a stop, not a finding

src: International Institute of Social History, Amsterdam — letter sent 9 Sep
what: The family tradition that he left Argentina as a communist on the run
got: Answered in a day, and the tradition is not supported there

src: Rosario cathedral register — the book, not the index
what: Testing the index against the acts behind it
got: Where that read began

src: Rosario, Indice de matrimonios — re-read at full resolution
what: Juan Carlos Lerena's marriage, where his wife's maiden name would be
got: Nothing, at a resolution that leaves no doubt

src: Rosario index, the whole L section
what: The last open corner, finished so it can be left behind
got: Closed

src: Nuestra Senora del Rosario cathedral, alphabetical index DGS 4530325
what: LERENA, every year 1882-1895
got: Fourteen consecutive years, nothing

src: Archivo General del Ejercito, Buenos Aires, and others
what: His libreta de enrolamiento, clase 1882, and other files
got: Some answered, some outstanding — the table says which

src: FamilySearch Spain: Baptisms 1502-1940, Catholic Church 1307-2005, Civil 1475-2005
what: The last of the four candidate birthplaces
got: Nothing

src: FamilySearch Uruguay: Civil Registration 1879-2020, Catholic Church 1726-2000, Baptisms 1750-1900, Index Cards 1900-1937
what: The successor to the Rosario work
got: Not him — but this is the corpus that later gave the Lerena Traibel their parentage

src: ancestors.co.za, All Deceased Estates 1994-2023 (gazette forms J193 and J187)
what: The surname alone
got: Estates found, with dates and gazette references

src: Rosario marriage index 1860-1904, L section, image 51
what: A line reading “Larena V · Sarmiento A” under Libro 9, 1884
got: Unresolved. Cannot be distinguished from Lavena, a real Rosario surname

src: FamilySearch, worldwide
what: Pablo Armando Lerena, fuzzy, births 1878-86
got: Two records exist on earth — his 1911 Cape marriage and a modern Find a Grave memorial

src: CEMLA and others
what: Lerena / Llerena / Larena / Lerina, 1800-1960
got: Run with David completing the CAPTCHAs at the keyboard. Others remain unreachable

src: The San Miguel baptisms of 1872 and other leads
what: Roberto Juan Roque Llorens and others
got: Unproven, and dropped. Kept so they are not chased twice

src: FamilySearch full-text search
what: The same null, asked a different way
got: Every null on this page is really one null: not in the index. Full text reaches only what has been keyed

src: Argentine marriages 1865-1885, and two more shapes
what: Juan Carlos Lerena, the day his name was found
got: Three more nulls

src: WikiTree
what: Added because it was asked for, and because the honest answer to “have you looked at WikiTree?” was no
got: Empty

src: Queensland Registry's own historical index, searched directly
what: The other Mary Ann Brayley, on whom a WikiTree claim turned
got: Run to ground. Searched at the registry rather than through anybody's re-hosting of it

src: FamilySearch, by forename rather than surname
what: Luis Eugenio Lerena Lenguas
got: The most useful thing learned here in a week — and it was learned by publishing a confident negative and being wrong within the hour

src: Three days of searching LERENA
what: The surname as a handle
got: It has hidden records three separate ways. The least reliable handle on this family

src: alex.onb.ac.at — the Austrian legal archive
what: Whether anything there could relate to the Lerenas
got: Nothing, and the question answered properly rather than waved away

src: Rosario confirmation register, read page by page, 15 May 1885 to 1897
what: Every entry names both parents, so an act for him would have named them
got: About two and a half thousand children, and no Lerena under seven spellings

src: FamilySearch full text, the surname spelled seven ways
what: Sancho Llerena, and then the name that matters
got: A method failure, a large payout, and then a controlled negative on the one name that matters

src: The variant sweep's own hits, opened one by one
what: Two that fired on Serena — the S-for-L this archive has documented five times
got: Both false, and one would have faked the answer

src: Rosario confirmations, opened for the first time
what: A confirmation act names the parents, and he was squarely in range
got: No Lerena in a sitting of 243 children. And a structure built from a sample of eleven, corrected

src: Trove — National Library of Australia, digitised newspapers
what: LERENA and LLERENA across the whole corpus
got: Nothing, and the control passed: 11,500 articles on South African racing, so the corpus could have held him
